instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, department_id), departments(id, dept_name)
Get employee names with their department names
output: SELECT e.name, d.dept_name FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id;

instruction:
Schema: orders(id, user_id, total), users(id, name)
Get all orders with user names
output: SELECT o.*, u.name FROM orders o JOIN users u ON o.user_id = u.id;

instruction:
Schema: orders(id, user_id, total), users(id, name)
Get all users even if they have no orders
output: SELECT u.name, o.total FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON u.id = o.user_id;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name), enrollments(student_id, course_id), courses(id, title)
Get student names with their course titles
output: SELECT s.name, c.title FROM students s JOIN enrollments e ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON e.course_id = c.id;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, manager_id)
Get employees with their manager names
output: SELECT e.name AS employee, m.name AS manager FROM employees e LEFT JOIN employees m ON e.manager_id = m.id;

instruction:
Schema: products(id, name, category_id), categories(id, cat_name)
Get product names with category names
output: SELECT p.name, c.cat_name FROM products p JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id;

instruction:
Schema: authors(id, name), books(id, title, author_id)
Get all authors including those without books
output: SELECT a.name, b.title FROM authors a LEFT JOIN books b ON a.id = b.author_id;

instruction:
Schema: customers(id, name), orders(id, customer_id, total)
Get customers who have never placed an order
output: SELECT c.name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.id IS NULL;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, dept_id), departments(id, dept_name)
Get department names even if no employees exist
output: SELECT d.dept_name, e.name FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.dept_id;

instruction:
Schema: users(id, name), roles(id, role_name), user_roles(user_id, role_id)
Get users with their role names
output: SELECT u.name, r.role_name FROM users u JOIN user_roles ur ON u.id = ur.user_id JOIN roles r ON ur.role_id = r.id;

instruction:
Schema: invoices(id, vendor_id, amount), vendors(id, name)
Get invoice amounts with vendor names for invoices over 1000
output: SELECT i.amount, v.name FROM invoices i JOIN vendors v ON i.vendor_id = v.id WHERE i.amount > 1000;

instruction:
Schema: posts(id, title, user_id), users(id, username)
Get post titles with usernames sorted by title
output: SELECT p.title, u.username FROM posts p JOIN users u ON p.user_id = u.id ORDER BY p.title;

instruction:
Schema: movies(id, title, director_id), directors(id, name)
Get all movies with director names using right join
output: SELECT m.title, d.name FROM directors d RIGHT JOIN movies m ON d.id = m.director_id;

instruction:
Schema: tags(id, tag_name), articles(id, title), article_tags(article_id, tag_id)
Get article titles with their tags
output: SELECT a.title, t.tag_name FROM articles a JOIN article_tags at ON a.id = at.article_id JOIN tags t ON at.tag_id = t.id;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, dept_id), departments(id, dept_name)
Get count of employees per department
output: SELECT d.dept_name, COUNT(e.id) FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_name;

instruction:
Schema: orders(id, customer_id, total), customers(id, name)
Get total spending per customer
output: SELECT c.name, SUM(o.total) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.name;

instruction:
Schema: students(id, name), grades(student_id, score)
Get students who scored above 90
output: SELECT DISTINCT s.name FROM students s JOIN grades g ON s.id = g.student_id WHERE g.score > 90;

instruction:
Schema: products(id, name, supplier_id), suppliers(id, company_name)
Get products with supplier company names where supplier is not null
output: SELECT p.name, s.company_name FROM products p JOIN suppliers s ON p.supplier_id = s.id;

instruction:
Schema: flights(id, origin_id, dest_id), airports(id, code)
Get flight origin and destination codes
output: SELECT f.id, o.code AS origin, d.code AS destination FROM flights f JOIN airports o ON f.origin_id = o.id JOIN airports d ON f.dest_id = d.id;

instruction:
Schema: employees(id, name, dept_id), departments(id, dept_name)
Get departments with more than 5 employees
output: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_name HAVING COUNT(e.id) > 5;

instruction:
Schema: users(id, name), sessions(user_id, login_at)
Get users with their latest login time
output: SELECT u.name, MAX(s.login_at) FROM users u JOIN sessions s ON u.id = s.user_id GROUP BY u.name;

instruction:
Schema: items(id, name, order_id), orders(id, order_date)
Get item names ordered after 2024-01-01
output: SELECT i.name FROM items i JOIN orders o ON i.order_id = o.id WHERE o.order_date > '2024-01-01';

instruction:
Schema: teachers(id, name), classes(id, subject, teacher_id)
Get teachers who teach no classes
output: SELECT t.name FROM teachers t LEFT JOIN classes c ON t.id = c.teacher_id WHERE c.id IS NULL;

instruction:
Schema: accounts(id, balance, branch_id), branches(id, city)
Get account balances with branch cities
output: SELECT a.balance, b.city FROM accounts a JOIN branches b ON a.branch_id = b.id;

instruction:
Schema: patients(id, name, doctor_id), doctors(id, name)
Get patient names with their doctor names
output: SELECT p.name AS patient, d.name AS doctor FROM patients p JOIN doctors d ON p.doctor_id = d.id;
